shoulderStatus: No flare reported. Cossacks 'a bit crackly' (the usual low-grade right-side crackle), lateral raise 'shoulder not hurting' territory — spotlight tempo work done clean.
lessonsForFutureWeeks: **Incline DB reached 55 on the last set with the slow eccentric intact — the pack-down survived, so the gate opened honestly.** Next week can open at 50 and bring 55 in for the last set or two again; don't jump all three sets to 55 until the pack-down holds across the whole lift.

**The lateral-raise spotlight proved the point: slowing the SAME 15lb made it genuinely hard.** 'Fine' at speed became 'really hard' with a slow up/down + 1s hold — needed a mid-set reset on the last set. When it rotates off spotlight, keep the tempo cue; the load doesn't need to move.

**Cable-column occupancy pushed the entire cable block onto rope/D-handle pulleys — this recurs.** Tri ext + straight-arm on a floor/kneeling rope pulley, cable lat raise on a D-handle pulley. The rope-pulley numbers (tri ext 42.5, straight-arm 62.5) are a DIFFERENT scale from cable column (70 / 120) — the workout should pre-populate the rope-pulley fallback number so he's not guessing when the column's taken. (Equipment Calibration Table updated.)

**Push press held 45 on ~1 min rest (half the prescribed 2 min) and still ran clean** — the floor's risen. He wants the next lever to be a slower eccentric, which matches the 🛑 tag (tempo before load). Give push press an explicit eccentric/pause cue next week rather than a number.

**Dip palm pressure has persisted two weeks.** Not a load or tempo problem per the standing note — it's hand position on the bars. Worth an explicit setup cue next push day (neutral wrist, weight through the heel of the palm / try a parallel-grip station if available).

notes: Long Coordination Gauntlet debuted and landed — 'super complex flow to learn, really fun, nailed it at the end.' Did 2 full rounds both sides on a 25lb bell; 'pretty cardio heavy and wore me out.' Two useful signals: (1) the WALTER CATCH is NOT the crux — the half-kneeling sub-sequence (getting into and out of the half-kneel, beats 9-12) is the confusing/hard part; I'd spotlighted the wrong move. (2) He questioned whether the half-kneeling windmill / half-kneeling tactical clean were 'a bit wrong,' then realized he might be misremembering — and the flow is in fact ACCURATE: beats 9-11 already describe the half-kneeling windmill, half-kneeling tactical clean, and the stand-up. His instinct about the moves was right; the flow already contains them. Appreciated strength running before the flow ('thanks for giving me the rest of the workout to work on this one').

exercises.context: 🌀 Debut — 14-move Conti flow, main block. Prescribed light bell, 2 rounds each side.

exercises.notes: Full 2 rounds both sides at 25lb — heavier than the 18-26 'light' framing but he owned it by the end. 'Super complex flow to learn, really fun.' It's genuinely cardio-heavy at 14 moves × 2 rounds × 2 sides. The learning-run framing worked: confusing at first, nailed by the end.

exercises.context: Beat 9 = HALF-KNEELING windmill; beat 10 = half-kneeling tactical clean; beat 11 = stand up. The half-kneeling sub-sequence.

sets.notes: 'The entire kneeling thing and getting into kneeling that's confusing.'

exercises.notes: This is the actual crux of the gauntlet, NOT the walter catch. The drop-to-half-kneel, the windmill/clean from the floor, and the stand-up (beats 9-12) are where the coordination load is — matches the flow's own flowNotes ('the tricky part is the half-kneeling sub-sequence'). The base exercise IDs (windmill, tactical-clean) understate it — the half-kneeling variant lives in the per-move notes. Facing cue since ADDED to beat 9 (user-confirmed): turn ~90° toward the raised arm going in, down knee out wide.

exercises.context: Beat 14, closes the gauntlet. I had spotlighted it as the crux.
exercises.notes: Explicitly NOT the hard part — my spotlight was misplaced. The soft two-hand catch at chest height was fine; the difficulty is upstream in the kneeling transitions.

exercises.context: 🔆 Warmup brain-primer spotlight — the figure-8 switch-clean he missed.
exercises.notes: Not separately called out in the report — folded into the session. It also appears twice inside the gauntlet (beats 2 and 12), so he got plenty of it either way.

shoulderStatus: Not separately reported. No flare called out across the overhead-heavy gauntlet (windmills, press, snatch, catch).
lessonsForFutureWeeks: **The gauntlet's crux is the HALF-KNEELING sub-sequence (beats 9-12), not the walter catch.** User: 'walter catch isn't the hard part, it's the entire kneeling thing and getting into kneeling that's confusing.' The flow's own flowNotes already say this ('the tricky part is the half-kneeling sub-sequence'). If this flow spotlights again, spotlight the kneeling drop-and-stand — that's where the coordination lives.

**Flow accuracy CONFIRMED — the half-kneeling windmill + half-kneeling tactical clean are already in the flow (beats 9-11) and correct.** He questioned it, then realized he might be misremembering. His read of the MOVES was right; his worry that the flow was 'wrong' was not. Resolved by reading the canonical bundle rather than acting on the uncertain correction.

**Facing cue now ADDED to beat 9 (user-confirmed W23D2).** Going into the half-kneel you turn ~90° toward the raised (overhead) arm and set the down knee out wide — that open sideways stance gives the kneeling windmill room. The fuller model (turning back to original facing at the walter catch) he hedged on and did not re-confirm, so it's deliberately NOT baked in.

**25lb was his working bell and 2 full rounds both sides was genuinely cardio-heavy** — 'wore me out.' For a 14-move × 2-round × 2-side flow, that's a real conditioning dose, not just skill practice. If it's meant to stay light-skill, 1 round or a lighter bell; he chose to push it and it worked.

**Strength-before-flow structure was appreciated** — 'thanks for giving me the rest of the workout to work on this one.' Running the strength block before the big flow (the anti-top-heavy structure) left him energy to actually learn the gauntlet. Keep that ordering for debut/complex flows.
